clue.text: A set of figures introduced by an associate is satisfactory

indicators.note: something introduced by another comes after it, so the friend's word goes in front

parts.note: a pal is a friend or associate
a table is a set of figures laid out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A spreadsheet presented by a colleague turns out to be good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palatable is acceptable or agreeable, as a satisfactory proposal is.

clue.text: Childless person getting an opportunity, perhaps

indicators.note: without a child, so the word son is removed from person

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: Someone without offspring gets a lucky break, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Childless' takes SON from person, leaving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for possibly or maybe.

clue.text: Frontier restriction

definitions.meaning: a cap or ceiling placed on something

explanation.definitionFit: A boundary line marks the edge of a territory, and a cap set on spending is the same word.

clue.text: Old Hebrew images show a Greek character sitting around

indicators.note: the session word goes around the letter and article

parts.note: a term is a session, a period when a court or parliament sits
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Ancient Jewish idols depict a Greek figure seated in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' wants to be a person; it is the letter PHI. 'show' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Household idols or cult figures mentioned in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Battle for a dog

definitions.meaning: a red-and-white breed of King Charles spaniel

explanation.definitionFit: Marlborough's 1704 victory gave its name to his palace and to a spaniel bred there.

clue.text: Achieve a result

definitions.meaning: to bring about, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to bring about a change; as a noun, the consequence of an action.

clue.text: Expression of contempt for money by author

parts.note: p, for penny or pence, is a unit of money
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright and author

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a writer who works only for the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disdain or impatience, like 'pooh' or 'bah'.

clue.text: Spinal trouble for Indians, for instance

indicators.note: trouble as disturb or stir up, so the letters of spinal are rearranged

explanation.surface: Back problems afflict Native Americans, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges SPINAL. The definition is loose: the Plains Indians are the peoples of the North American Great Plains, so 'Indians, for instance' points to the word that describes them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Plains of North America were home to the Sioux and Cheyenne, so those Indians are an example of the grassland word.

clue.text: When one can often get bitter quite reasonably!

definitions.text: When one can often get bitter quite reasonably!

parts.words: When one can often get bitter quite reasonably!
parts.note: reads as a time when someone turns resentful with good reason; bitter is a British draught beer sold cheaply in pubs early in the evening

explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like resentful; it is the hoppy British beer, and 'reasonably' means cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's early-evening period of cut-price drinks.

clue.text: "So runs the away" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word completes Hamlet's line after the play scene, 'So runs the ... away'

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash for the missing word between 'the' and 'away'; Hamlet says it in Act 3, Scene 2.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in Hamlet's line means the earth, everything that exists.

clue.text: A part of the military code to regret?

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
Morse is the dot-and-dash signalling code

explanation.surface: A question of whether some army unit's rulebook makes room for repentance.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sorrow or guilt over a past wrong; the noun sense of regret.

clue.text: Lively young lady — or a bird!

definitions.meaning: a fashionable, high-spirited young woman of the 1920s
a young wild duck or partridge just able to flutter its wings

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from flapping: the 1920s good-time girl and a fledgling duck or partridge still learning to fly.

clue.text: Excited, he starts to talk utter poppycock

indicators.note: the starts of the next three words, their opening letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A man gets worked up and begins to spout complete nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial for agitated or worked up, as an excited person is.

clue.text: London borough journalist is overworked

parts.note: Hackney is a borough in east London
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter in an inner-city London district is run off their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Overworked here means overused and trite, as a stale phrase is.

clue.text: Resit in university resolved the complaint

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken up and reformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student retaking an exam at college clears up an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges RESIT, IN and U (university). 'Resolved' reads as settled, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of a nerve is a medical condition, which crosswords often call a complaint.

clue.text: Found out about judge's having no precedent

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the judge's word
out as in wrong or disordered, so the letters of found are rearranged

parts.note: to hear a case is what a judge does

explanation.surface: Someone discovers something about a judge's ruling that has never happened before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found out' reads as discovered, but 'out' is the anagram signal on Found, and 'about' wraps the shuffled letters round the judge's verb; a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something never known or done before has no earlier example to follow.

clue.text: Urge to return to an African village

indicators.note: returning in a down-to-across sense here: the word for urge is read backwards

parts.note: to prod someone is to urge them on

explanation.surface: Someone feels a pull to go back to a small settlement in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns PROD round. A dorp is a small town or village in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans word for a small rural town or village in South Africa.

clue.text: Completed training, was accepted and then rejected

parts.note: passed, as a motion or bill passes when approved
out, as in voted out or thrown out

explanation.surface: A recruit finished the course, got through, and was then turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets parade on finishing their military course, which marks the end of their instruction.

clue.text: Heart-warming applause

explanation.definitionFit: Good news is uplifting, and a crowd's shouts of approval are the same word as a noun.

clue.text: Whimsical desire, exactly stated

indicators.note: stated means spoken, so the words for desire and exactly are said aloud

parts.note: fancy means desire, and full means exactly, as in hit full in the face

explanation.surface: A capricious wish, precisely put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desire' gives FANCY and 'exactly' gives FULL, which said together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Imaginative and unrealistic, given to flights of fancy.

clue.text: Close imitation of a nymph

definitions.meaning: a faithful repetition or copy of something
the mountain nymph of Greek myth who pined away until only her voice remained

explanation.definitionFit: A reverberating sound repeats what was said, and the Greek nymph who loved Narcissus was left as a repeating voice.

clue.text: Her taste developed in military areas

indicators.note: developed as something that has changed shape and grown, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman acquires a liking for life around army bases.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is a region where military operations take place.

clue.text: Write article on Grand Island

parts.note: to pen is to write
an is the indefinite article
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone writes a piece about a large island.
explanation.definitionFit: An island off the west coast of Malaysia, home of George Town.

clue.text: Take meal without a formal introduction

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the meal word goes around the letter

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats a meal without being properly introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, so LUNCH goes around A. 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The official unveiling of a new product or ship, a public debut.

clue.text: Stand-off half —- best with a couple of drinks

indicators.note: half of the word best: its back half, the last two of its four letters

parts.note: ale is beer
maté is a South American herbal tea

explanation.surface: A rugby fly-half is at his best after a pint or two.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a stand-off half is a back position, so 'Stand-off half' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Stand-off' alone. 'half' takes ST from best.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock in which neither side can win, as in chess when no legal move remains.

clue.text: Scrap metal is stowed in a vessel

indicators.note: stored inside, so the metal goes inside the vessel

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
Cr is the chemical symbol for chromium, a metal

explanation.surface: Junk metal is kept aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel or abandon it.

clue.text: Class found by word of mouth

indicators.note: spoken, so the word for found is said aloud

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: Someone's social standing is discovered through gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past of find; here it is the verb meaning to cast metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, especially in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Young man at odds with doctor

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds when a race begins
to rig is to fiddle or doctor something

explanation.surface: A youth disagrees with his physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician; it is the verb meaning to falsify. 'at odds' reads as disagreeing, but odds alone gives SP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a youth or young lad, a slightly dismissive term.

clue.text: Report left out and pinched, so written again

indicators.note: with this word taken out of the word report

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a pinched face looks drawn, thin and strained

explanation.surface: An account omitted and then stolen, so it had to be produced afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes PORT (left) from Report, leaving RE. 'pinched' wants to mean stolen; it is the gaunt look.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn once more, as a map or document is when it is recreated.

clue.text: Torture of inner hell

indicators.note: torture as twisting out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The torments suffered deep within the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's name for the underworld, a blazing pit of the damned.

clue.text: The Old Contemptibles go back muddy

parts.note: the nickname of the British Expeditionary Force (BEF) of 1914

indicators.note: going back, so the word go is read in reverse

explanation.surface: First World War veterans retreat through the mire.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1914 British Expeditionary Force took the name Old Contemptibles from a reputed jibe by the Kaiser. 'muddy' is a verb: to cloud or confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to obscure or confuse, as muddied thinking is clouded.

clue.text: Draw attention to excessive entertaining

parts.note: high, as in high prices, means excessive
light, as in light entertainment, means easy and amusing

explanation.surface: Someone points out that a show is overdoing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise or spotlight something so that it stands out.
